ic_name: TIA/EIA-485 (RS-485 via TI SLLA272C Design Guide)
protocol_type: Electrical-only physical-layer standard. RS-485 has NO command set, NO frame format, NO addressing — it defines only the driver/receiver electricals and bus topology. Framing / addressing / CRC are layered on top by higher-level protocols (Modbus RTU, DL/T645, BACnet MS/TP, etc.).

channels_2_wire_half_duplex.name: A
channels_2_wire_half_duplex.description: Non-inverting differential bus line. When the active driver transmits a logical '1' (mark), A is the more positive of the pair.

channels_2_wire_half_duplex.name: B
channels_2_wire_half_duplex.description: Inverting differential bus line. When the active driver transmits a logical '1' (mark), B is the more negative of the pair.

channels_2_wire_half_duplex.name: GND-ref
channels_2_wire_half_duplex.description: Common ground reference between nodes; in long links with ground-potential differences, isolation is required.

channels_4_wire_full_duplex.name: Y
channels_4_wire_full_duplex.description: Non-inverting transmit pair line out of the master driver.

channels_4_wire_full_duplex.name: Z
channels_4_wire_full_duplex.description: Inverting transmit pair line out of the master driver.

channels_4_wire_full_duplex.name: A
channels_4_wire_full_duplex.description: Non-inverting receive pair line into the master receiver (and into each slave transmitter for upstream).

channels_4_wire_full_duplex.name: B
channels_4_wire_full_duplex.description: Inverting receive pair line into the master receiver.

transceiver_digital_pins.name: D / DI
transceiver_digital_pins.description: Driver input from the host UART (TXD). Determines A/B differential polarity when driver is enabled.

transceiver_digital_pins.name: DE
transceiver_digital_pins.description: Driver Enable, active HIGH. When DE=1 the transceiver drives A/B; when DE=0 the driver outputs are high-impedance (tri-stated).

transceiver_digital_pins.name: RE#
transceiver_digital_pins.description: Receiver Enable, active LOW. When RE#=0 the receiver output R is driven; when RE#=1 R is high-impedance.

transceiver_digital_pins.name: R / RO
transceiver_digital_pins.description: Receiver output to the host UART (RXD). Reflects the logical bus state when receiver enabled.

rows: Receiver R = undetermined unless fail-safe biasing forces a determined state

valid_ready_handshake_rules: There is no per-byte VALID/READY handshake on the differential bus — RS-485 is an asynchronous electrical layer.
Half-duplex direction handover requires software-controlled DE / RE# coordination — only one driver may be enabled at any time to avoid bus contention.
Higher-level protocols (Modbus RTU master/slave, DL/T645 request/reply) provide application-level request/response handshaking and per-message timing rules (e.g. Modbus RTU 3.5-char inter-frame gap).
Receiver fail-safe biasing acts as a passive 'idle = mark' handshake when no driver is active.
byte_oriented: byte-stream when wrapping UART framing (most common); pure bit-stream otherwise.

frame_format.note: RS-485 does NOT define a frame format. The most common usage wraps RS-422-style UART framing (start bit + 5..9 data bits + optional parity + stop bit) on top of the differential bus, then higher protocols (Modbus RTU, DMX-512, …) frame those bytes into messages.
